literal_meaning: ঈশ্বরীয় বা আল্লাহর রাত (divine or Allah's night)
figurative_meaning_bn: মহরমের জাগরণের রাত; যে রাত আর শেষ হতে চায় না
figurative_meaning_en: The night of vigil during Muharram; a night that seems unwilling to end
similar_in_english: the longest night of the year
example_sentences_in_bangla: মহরমের এই ইলাহী রাতে সবাই জাগরণে মগ্ন।
আজকের ইলাহী রাত কোনোমতে শেষ হলো না।
example_sentences_in_english: During this Ilahi night of Muharram, everyone is immersed in vigil.
Tonight's Ilahi night just wouldn't end.
history: This idiom refers to the vigils held during Muharram, commemorating the martyrdom of Imam Hussein at the Battle of Karbala in 680 CE, a pivotal event in Shia Islam observed by Bengali Muslims.
note: Primarily used in Muslim Bengali communities during religious observances.
